question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Surat Factory — Location / Coastal Identity]
options: Surat — Located on the banks of the Tapti River in Gujarat
Surat — Major port on the western (Arabian Sea) coast of India
Surat — First English factory in India established in 1613
Surat — Located on the Coromandel (eastern) coast of India
wrong_fact: Surat is on India's western coast (Arabian Sea / Gujarat), NOT on the Coromandel (eastern) coast.
explanation: Surat is situated on the western coast of India in present-day Gujarat, on the banks of the Tapti River, and opens onto the Arabian Sea. The Coromandel coast refers to the southeastern coast of India (modern Tamil Nadu/Andhra Pradesh). The English established their first permanent factory at Surat in 1613 after Emperor Jahangir issued a farman, making it India's first English trading post — but always on the western, not eastern, coast.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Surat Factory — Key Persons / Events]
options: Captain William Hawkins — Arrived at Surat in 1608 seeking trading rights from Jahangir
Thomas Best — Defeated Portuguese fleet off Swally (Suvali) near Surat in 1612
Francis Day — Received the imperial farman allowing the Surat factory in 1613
Thomas Aldworth — First President of the Surat factory established in 1613
wrong_fact: It was NOT Francis Day who received the farman for Surat. Francis Day is associated with Madras (1639). The Surat factory rights were secured by the Company after Thomas Best's naval victory, and Thomas Aldworth became its first President.
explanation: The naval victory of Thomas Best over the Portuguese at the Battle of Swally (1612) near Surat persuaded Emperor Jahangir to grant the English trading rights. Thomas Aldworth was appointed the first President of the Surat factory (1613). Francis Day is a completely different figure — he obtained the lease for Madraspatnam (future Madras/Fort St. George) in 1639, on the eastern coast. Confusing Day with Surat is a classic mismatch.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Surat Factory — Administrative & Trade Role]
options: Surat — Functioned as the headquarters of the English Company on the western coast until 1687
Surat — The English President at Surat initially had jurisdiction over all English factories in India
Surat — Lost primacy to Bombay as the western-coast HQ after Bombay's development under Gerald Aungier
Surat — Was transferred from Mughal to English control via the Treaty of Purandar (1665)
wrong_fact: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was between the Mughals and Maratha Shivaji — it had nothing to do with transferring Surat to English control. Surat remained a Mughal-controlled city; the English only operated a factory there under Mughal permission.
explanation: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was a Mughal-Maratha agreement by which Shivaji ceded many of his forts to the Mughals, not a treaty involving the English at Surat. Surat was a Mughal imperial port city; the English traded there by permission (farman). Bombay — received by Charles II as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry in 1661 and handed to the Company in 1668 — gradually replaced Surat as the English western-coast headquarters, a shift completed by 1687 when the presidency was formally moved.
